entries.description: The Weasleys’ former Ford Anglia is described as running wild in the Forbidden Forest.
entries.model_notes: A mobile inhabitant of the Forest at this date, not a fixed parked vehicle or a constraint on the Forest’s dimensions.

entries.description: Hermione explains that Muggles see Hogwarts as a deteriorating ruin with an entrance warning declaring it dangerous and unsafe to enter.
entries.temporal: September 1994; described as an existing enchantment
entries.model_notes: Character explanation, attributed to her reading of Hogwarts: A History. This defines a Muggle-facing appearance; it does not establish that the actual castle is ruined. The subsequent Unplottability discussion concerns Durmstrang, not a confirmed Hogwarts property.

entries.description: The Hogwarts Express departs the concealed platform nine and three-quarters at King’s Cross, travels north, and arrives at Hogsmeade station after dark. The London platform is accessed through the apparently solid barrier between platforms nine and ten.
entries.model_notes: Regional approach context only. No travel distance or exact bearing beyond northward travel is given.

entries.description: At the stormy evening arrival, Hagrid waits at the far end of the platform. First-years traditionally sail across the lake to the castle; approximately a hundred apparently horseless carriages wait outside the station and carry the other pupils up a track towards Hogwarts.
entries.model_notes: Retain Harry’s perception of horseless carriages. The paragraph gives the upward route and approximate vehicle count, not the track’s measured length or the lake landing geometry.

entries.description: Carriages pass through gates flanked by winged-boar statues and climb a sweeping drive to the great oak front doors above a flight of stone steps. Many illuminated castle windows are visible through the rain.
entries.model_notes: Preserve the ordered station–gates–drive–steps–front-doors approach. No count of steps, gate material, or precise drive curvature is supplied.

entries.description: The Entrance Hall is cavernous and torch-lit and contains a magnificent marble staircase. Peeves hovers twenty feet above arriving pupils; water balloons leave the floor wet and slippery.
entries.model_notes: The hovering height supplies at least that much clearance at his position, not a measured ceiling height. Wetness belongs to this incident.

entries.description: Double doors on the right of the Entrance Hall lead into the Great Hall.
entries.model_notes: The right-hand relation is given on entering via the front doors; preserve that viewpoint.

entries.description: Hundreds of candles float above four long student house tables. Golden plates and goblets stand on the tables; at the top of the Hall the staff sit along one side of a fifth table facing the pupils. Harry’s route passes Slytherin, Ravenclaw and Hufflepuff before reaching Gryffindor at the far side, with Slytherin subsequently described across the Hall.
entries.model_notes: Record the observed traversal and opposite-side relation without assuming equal table spacing. The tablecloth is white linen; spilled pumpkin juice stains it during this meal.

entries.description: Flitwick sits on a large pile of cushions beside Sprout, who is beside Sinistra; Snape is on Sinistra’s other side. A vacant seat separates Snape from Dumbledore at the centre. The arriving Moody is given the seat on Dumbledore’s right, while Hagrid sits at an end of the table.
entries.model_notes: A dated seating arrangement. Harry guesses that the vacant seat is McGonagall’s; do not treat that identification as directly observed or fix all seating permanently.

entries.description: The enchanted ceiling shows the outdoor sky: swirling black and purple storm clouds and flashes of lightning. High dark windows admit the sound of heavy rain and shake with thunder.
entries.model_notes: Separate the magical visible sky from the actual roof structure, whose construction and height are not specified.

entries.description: The first-years line up along the staff table facing the rest of the school. McGonagall places the ancient patched Sorting Hat on a three-legged stool in front of them and removes both when the Sorting ends.
entries.model_notes: A removable start-of-term installation, not a permanent obstruction.

entries.description: Hagrid enters through a door behind the teachers’ table.
entries.model_notes: The door’s destination and dimensions are unstated; keep a usable connection without inventing its route.

entries.description: Dennis reports falling into the lake and being pushed back into the boat by something underwater. Colin suggests the giant squid; the narration describes the lake as fathoms deep.
entries.model_notes: The rescue is a character report; the squid identification is speculation. Fathoms deep is qualitative, not a mapped bathymetric measurement.

entries.description: Empty dishes fill with food without visible delivery. The first course vanishes and is instantly replaced by puddings, and remaining crumbs later disappear leaving clean plates.
entries.model_notes: Allow magical food-state changes at the tables. These paragraphs do not establish the mechanism or the kitchen’s position.

entries.description: Nearly Headless Nick reports that Peeves threw pots and pans around and left the kitchens flooded with soup before the feast.
entries.model_notes: A reported disruption earlier the same evening, not the normal kitchen state.

entries.description: Nearly Headless Nick says Hogwarts has over a hundred house-elves, normally in the kitchens by day, emerging at night to clean and attend to fires.
entries.model_notes: The stated count and work pattern are reported. They imply staffing and nighttime activity, not a proven kitchen capacity or plan.

entries.description: Dumbledore says the castle’s list of about 437 prohibited objects can be consulted in Filch’s office.
entries.model_notes: Provides a displayed or consultable office list; its mounting and format are unstated.

entries.description: Dumbledore reminds pupils that the Forest within the grounds is out of bounds and Hogsmeade is barred to pupils below third year.
entries.model_notes: Institutional access rules at this date, not an impassable physical barrier.

entries.location: Route to Gryffindor Tower: concealed staircase
entries.description: On the route from the Entrance Hall towards Gryffindor Tower the group passes through a door hidden behind a tapestry and climbs a narrower staircase. A step halfway up lets Neville’s foot sink through; a suit of armour at the top laughs, and Ron closes its visor.
entries.model_notes: No intervening route or floor number is given. The narration calls this one of many Hogwarts trick stairs; model this local trap without making every staircase identical.

entries.location: Gryffindor Tower entrance and common room
entries.description: A large portrait of the Fat Lady in pink silk hides the entrance. After the password she swings forward to expose a hole in the wall. The circular common room has a crackling fire, squashy armchairs, tables, and a doorway to the girls’ dormitories.
entries.model_notes: Password at this visit is Balderdash. Retain a climb-through wall opening and a separate girls’ dormitory doorway; the opening’s exact height is unspecified.

entries.description: A final spiral staircase reaches the boys’ dormitory at the top of the Tower. Five four-poster beds with deep crimson hangings stand against the walls, trunks at their feet. Bedside tables and headboards support Dean’s Krum and West Ham posters and Seamus’s Ireland rosette; warming pans have been placed in the sheets.
entries.model_notes: Specific to this dormitory and date. Harry attributes the warming pans to house-elves without witnessing placement; do not infer other dormitories’ bed counts.

entries.description: The ceiling displays pewter-grey clouds after the storm; around a hundred owls fly through the open windows and circle the house tables delivering post.
entries.model_notes: Establishes functional window entry for a large owl flight; the owl count is approximate and does not give window dimensions.

entries.description: The pupils cross a sodden vegetable path to greenhouse three, where black slug-like Bubotubers protrude upright from soil and produce a petrol-smelling yellow-green liquid when squeezed.
entries.model_notes: Keep the source wording vegetable path; its exact planting layout is not established. The plants and collecting bottles are a dated lesson installation.

entries.description: A booming castle bell is audible in the grounds. After Herbology the Hufflepuffs go up stone steps for Transfiguration, while the Gryffindors head in the other direction down a sloping lawn towards Hagrid’s small wooden cabin at the Forbidden Forest edge. They later walk back uphill to the castle for lunch.
entries.model_notes: Defines relative slope and route branching, not an immediate adjacency between the greenhouse and the Transfiguration classroom.

entries.description: Several open wooden crates stand on the ground outside the cabin, each containing about a hundred newly hatched six-inch Blast-Ended Skrewts. The area has a rotting-fish smell, rattles, small explosions and sparks.
entries.model_notes: A dated teaching setup; creature counts are approximate. Crates can be approached from the outside lesson area.

entries.description: At the top of a tightly spiralling staircase in North Tower a silver stepladder leads through a circular ceiling trapdoor into Trelawney’s room.
entries.model_notes: Preserve both the staircase and the ladder stage. The route to North Tower and its exact floor level are unspecified.

entries.description: The circular room has closed curtains, dim reddish light from many lamps covered with scarves and shawls, and a sweet-smelling hot fire. Chintz chairs and pouffes crowd the space around small circular tables. Trelawney sits in a large winged armchair before the fire facing the class.
entries.model_notes: Furnish densely while retaining paths through occupied seating. Closed curtains describe the customary state here, not a lack of windows.

entries.description: After Divination the pupils descend staircases towards dinner in the Great Hall and reach the Entrance Hall, where pupils queue.
entries.model_notes: A descending route is explicit; the text does not enumerate the flights or establish a direct single stair.

entries.location: Entrance Hall floor and dungeon access
entries.description: The Entrance Hall floor is stone-flagged. The marble staircase descends into the Hall; from here Malfoy moves towards the dungeons, and Moody later escorts him that way to see Snape. Footsteps and shouts echo in the Hall.
entries.model_notes: Dungeon access is connected to the Hall but its doorway position and intervening steps are unstated. The magical ferret incident adds no permanent architectural damage.

entries.location: Defence Against the Dark Arts classroom
entries.description: Pupils have chairs and desks, including three seats directly before the teacher’s wooden desk. Moody stores a jar of spiders in a desk drawer and conducts demonstrations on its top. A blackboard stands within Harry’s line of sight from the front seats.
entries.model_notes: The pupils’ desk is solid wood; the teacher’s desktop is also explicitly wooden. The mention of throwing a spider from a window is a hypothetical action, not a demonstrated exit.

entries.description: After leaving the classroom, the pupils find Neville halfway along a side passage opposite a stone wall. Moody meets them there, offers to take Neville up to his office to see books, and leads him away around a corner.
entries.model_notes: Preserve a nearby branching passage and corner. Up to the office is Moody’s wording, not a fully traced stair route; books in the office are reported.

entries.description: A moonlit window-sill can support Hedwig outside the common room. Harry opens the window; she flies across the room to a table and later leaves through the opening.
entries.model_notes: An operable exterior window with a sill and clear flight path. No compass bearing, size, or elevation is given.

entries.description: Harry directs Hedwig up to the Owlery for food.
entries.model_notes: Reports the Owlery’s feeding function and Harry’s upward direction, not a directly observed feeder or exact route.

entries.description: Harry leaves the portrait hole and makes his way upwards through the castle, passing a large vase halfway along the fourth-floor corridor, to the Owlery at the top of West Tower.
entries.model_notes: Preserve the narrated route despite any assumed floor relationships; it does not enumerate every stair or identify where the climb begins. Peeves attempts to tip the vase during this visit.

entries.description: The Owlery is a circular stone room with unglazed window openings and cold draughts. Straw, owl droppings, and regurgitated mouse and vole skeletons cover the slippery floor. Perches rise nearly to the top of the tower and hold hundreds of owls. Harry takes Hedwig to a wall opening and watches her fly into the sunrise.
entries.model_notes: No fixed compass direction is given for a particular opening; the sunrise is a sightline in this scene. Different owl breeds share the perches.

entries.location: Defence Against the Dark Arts classroom
entries.description: Moody moves the classroom desks aside with his wand, leaving a large clear central area for Imperius practice. A desk remains close enough for Harry to collide with and knock over.
entries.model_notes: A movable teaching layout, with no dimensions or reported structural damage.

entries.description: A large tournament notice is erected at the foot of the marble staircase, where the crowd reading it obstructs passage through the Entrance Hall. It directs pupils to assemble in front of the castle for the foreign delegations’ arrival.
entries.model_notes: A temporary freestanding or erected sign; construction is unstated. Its announced date is 30 October.

entries.description: Before the guests arrive, grimy portraits are scrubbed and their subjects appear pink-faced and uncomfortable. Suits of armour are polished until they gleam and move without squeaking.
entries.model_notes: A cleaning state transition affecting existing furnishings; the individual frames and armour positions are not given.

entries.description: Enormous silk house banners hang on the Hall walls: red with a gold lion, blue with a bronze eagle, yellow with a black badger, and green with a silver serpent. The largest banner, behind the staff table, bears the combined Hogwarts arms around an H.
entries.model_notes: Retain the stated bronze Ravenclaw eagle and the location of the larger school banner.

entries.description: Hermione describes house-elves changing bed sheets, lighting fires, cleaning classrooms and cooking food. George says he and Fred have repeatedly visited the kitchens for food.
entries.model_notes: Reported servicing and student kitchen access. This passage supplies no kitchen entrance route.

entries.description: Pupils file down the front steps and stand in rows in front of the castle, with the drive descending towards the front gates. From the top of the lawns they overlook the grounds and have a clear view of the lake’s surface. The moon is seen over the Forest; light streams outside from the Entrance Hall and front doors.
entries.model_notes: Use these specific viewpoints and relative slopes without inferring compass bearings or that every part of the shore is visible.

entries.description: Hermione states that Apparition cannot be performed inside the Hogwarts grounds.
entries.model_notes: A reported magical boundary condition; no perimeter dimensions or exception mechanism is supplied.

entries.description: A house-sized powder-blue carriage flies over the Forest canopy and lands near the waiting pupils outside the castle. It has enormous wheels, a door emblazoned with crossed golden wands each emitting three stars, and fold-out golden steps. Twelve winged palomino horses, each elephant-sized, draw it.
entries.model_notes: Temporary guest transport and its landing clearance. The exact standing position after arrival is not yet specified.

entries.description: Madame Maxime says her powerful horses require forceful handling and drink only single-malt whisky; Dumbledore assigns Hagrid to their care.
entries.model_notes: Reported care requirement useful for the later temporary paddock; no stable is established here.

entries.description: Rumbling and sucking sounds precede bubbles, waves spilling over muddy banks, and a whirlpool in the middle of the lake. A mast, rigging and skeletal-looking ship rise from it; dim misty lights shine at the portholes. Once fully afloat the ship glides to shore, drops anchor in the shallows, and lowers a plank onto the bank. The delegation walks uphill across the lawns to the castle.
entries.model_notes: A temporary magical arrival and mooring, not evidence for a permanent lake drain. No actual underwater route or external origin is visible.

entries.description: Beauxbatons pupils sit at the Ravenclaw table and Durmstrang at Slytherin. Filch adds four staff chairs, two on either side of Dumbledore: Maxime sits to his left with Crouch beyond her, and Bagman sits beyond Karkaroff on the other side. The ceiling shows a black starry sky.
entries.model_notes: A dated additional seating state; do not permanently enlarge the normal staff complement.

entries.description: Filch brings an ancient-looking wooden chest encrusted with jewels to the table before Dumbledore. Three wand taps open its creaking lid; Dumbledore removes the large roughly hewn wooden Goblet, filled with blue-white flames, and displays it on the closed chest.
entries.model_notes: Portable tournament equipment, large enough to be seen across the Hall.

entries.description: Karkaroff directs his students back to the ship after the feast and offers to send mulled wine from the kitchens.
entries.model_notes: Reported use of the ship as guest accommodation, rather than a Hogwarts dormitory allocation. No cabins are described.

entries.location: Entrance Hall Goblet and Age Line
entries.description: The Goblet stands in the centre of the Entrance Hall on the stool normally used for the Sorting Hat. A thin golden circle is marked on the floor ten feet around it in every direction. Dumbledore says under-seventeens cannot cross; Fred and George’s Ageing Potion fails and the line ejects them onto the cold stone floor ten feet away, giving them white beards. Names dropped into the Goblet briefly turn its blue-white fire red and produce sparks.
entries.model_notes: Preserve both the stated ten-foot extent around the Goblet and the separately stated ejection distance. Neither should be silently converted into a ten-foot diameter. The age restriction is explained and then observed.

entries.description: Dumbledore tells the bearded twins to go up to Madam Pomfrey, and they depart for the hospital wing.
entries.model_notes: An upward direction is reported; the scene does not trace the stairs or specify the hospital floor.

entries.description: Live bats fly around the enchanted ceiling and hundreds of carved pumpkins occupy the Hall’s corners. For the selection ceremony Dumbledore extinguishes all candles except those in the pumpkins, leaving semi-darkness dominated by the bright Goblet.
entries.model_notes: Dated lighting and decorations. The text does not state explicitly whether the previous house banners have been removed.

entries.description: The carriage is parked two hundred yards from Hagrid’s front door near the Forest edge. Students climb inside it, and its winged horses graze in a makeshift paddock alongside.
entries.model_notes: A measured separation from the cabin front door, without a compass bearing. The temporary paddock is adjacent to the carriage.

entries.location: Hagrid’s pumpkin patch and Skrewt boxes
entries.description: Hagrid says the surviving Skrewts, now nearly three feet long and about twenty in number, are kept in separate boxes out by the pumpkin patch because they have begun killing one another.
entries.model_notes: Reported dated husbandry arrangement; the pumpkin patch’s distance or orientation relative to the cabin is unspecified.

entries.description: The cabin contains a single room with a gigantic patchwork-covered bed in one corner, a chest of drawers beside it, and an enormous wooden table and chairs before the fire. Cured hams and dead birds hang from the ceiling over the table. Rain is audible at the window.
entries.model_notes: Explicit single-room plan; retain oversized furnishings while leaving actual dimensions unassigned.

entries.description: A water barrel stands outside the cabin window. From inside, Harry and his friends see Hagrid washing at it and see Maxime and her pupils emerging from their carriage; they can see Hagrid speaking to Maxime but cannot hear the conversation.
entries.model_notes: Connect this particular cabin window with barrel and carriage sightlines; the two-hundred-yard carriage distance does not prove every part of that view is equally distant.

entries.location: Cabin and lake to castle routes
entries.description: From Hagrid’s cabin the pupils walk uphill over sloping lawns towards the castle. They see the Durmstrang party also coming uphill from the lake and entering the castle front doors ahead of them.
entries.model_notes: Two approaches converge on the front entrance. Neither exact junction nor path surfacing is given.

entries.description: For selection the Goblet is moved from the Entrance Hall to the staff table before Dumbledore’s chair. Champions are instructed to go along the staff table into the next chamber through the door behind it; Krum turns right at the table to reach it. Fleur walks between Ravenclaw and Hufflepuff; Hufflepuff is the next table from Gryffindor.
entries.model_notes: Krum’s right turn is from his approach towards the staff table. These are local route constraints, not a complete overhead seating plan.

entries.description: Harry walks between Gryffindor and Hufflepuff to the staff table, passes Hagrid’s end seat and enters the smaller room beyond the rear door. Great Hall voices are audible when its door is open.
entries.model_notes: A contiguous route and acoustic connection. The perceived very long walk is subjective, not a distance measurement.

entries.description: Paintings of witches and wizards line the smaller room. A roaring fireplace with a mantelpiece is opposite the entrance, and a candle-filled chandelier hangs low enough for Maxime’s head to brush it. Some parts of the room beyond the firelight remain in shadow.
entries.model_notes: Maxime’s height is not measured here, so the chandelier contact gives a relational clearance only.

entries.description: A wizened witch moves from her painting into the adjacent frame containing a walrus-moustached wizard. Later the same witch, identified as Violet, shares the Fat Lady’s portrait at Gryffindor Tower.
entries.model_notes: Observed movement and shared frames establish portrait travel. The specific route through every picture on seven staircases is Harry’s reconstruction rather than a witnessed sequence.

entries.location: Great Hall and Entrance Hall after selection
entries.description: The deserted Great Hall is lit by low-burning candles inside carved pumpkins, whose jagged mouths flicker. The Entrance Hall has only torchlight after the Goblet’s removal.
entries.model_notes: Late Hallowe’en lighting state; does not mean permanent candles are absent elsewhere in the building.

entries.location: Entrance Hall door beside marble staircase
entries.description: Cedric takes a door to the right of the marble staircase and descends stone steps beyond it, while Harry climbs the marble staircase towards Gryffindor.
entries.model_notes: This is Cedric’s departure towards his house celebrations; the text does not yet explicitly identify the steps’ destination. Do not conflate the door with the Great Hall’s right-hand entrance.

entries.description: Ron closes the hangings around his four-poster; they are dark red velvet.
entries.model_notes: Adds the curtain material to the earlier crimson-colour description; the curtains can conceal an occupant.

entries.description: Harry and Hermione descend from Gryffindor, cross the Entrance Hall, and walk across the lawns to the lake and moored Durmstrang ship. Owls occupy a nearby tree. A large tentacle rises from the lake to take a piece of toast floating on the surface.
entries.model_notes: The tentacle is observed; this passage does not directly name its owner or establish a permanent feeding point.

entries.description: The Owlery has long lines of perches, straw on the floor, and high rafters to which Hedwig can fly out of reach. School owls are kept here; Hermione says anyone may borrow them.
entries.model_notes: Observed structure and stock, with unrestricted borrowing as Hermione’s report. No count of school-owned versus privately owned owls is established.

entries.description: Pupils share a tray while re-potting Bouncing Bulbs in Herbology; the bulbs can wriggle free and strike nearby pupils.
entries.model_notes: A specific lesson installation. The passage does not name its greenhouse or establish that it is the same room as the earlier Bubotubers.

entries.location: Hagrid’s cabin and Skrewt exercise lawn
entries.description: Hagrid brings individual Skrewt crates from behind his cabin. Pupils take the now armoured, over-three-foot Skrewts on leashes across the lawn, scattering widely as the creatures blast forward several yards at a time.
entries.model_notes: A dated outdoor lesson. The crates come from behind the cabin, not explicitly from an interior room or shed.

entries.description: During Summoning practice Hermione draws board dusters, wastepaper baskets and Lunascopes across Flitwick’s classroom.
entries.model_notes: Identifies classroom equipment and room-crossing paths but gives no quantities or storage arrangement.

entries.description: A dim underground stone passage runs outside Snape’s dungeon; voices echo in it. Within the classroom pupils sit at tables and desks, with Snape’s desk at the front and seating extending to the back and across the room.
entries.model_notes: No fixed seating map is supplied. The badge lights brighten the passage during this incident, not as permanent illumination.

entries.description: Harry and Colin leave the dungeon towards steps leading into the Entrance Hall, then reach the classroom used for the Wand Weighing. Harry later goes down from that room to dinner.
entries.model_notes: The route establishes an ascent from the dungeon and a later descent to dinner; it does not enumerate the intermediate flights or identify the weighing room’s floor.

entries.description: A fairly small classroom is rearranged with most desks at the back, a large central clearing, and three desks end-to-end beneath a long velvet covering before the blackboard. Five chairs stand behind them for judges; champions sit near the door. It has an open window through which conjured birds fly into daylight.
entries.model_notes: The photographer cannot stand far enough back to frame Maxime standing, but lens and framing are unknown; do not derive a numeric room width from that problem.

entries.description: A nearby door opens into a cramped broom cupboard. Rita seats herself on an upturned bucket and Harry on a cardboard box, using a crate of Mrs Skower’s cleaning fluid as a writing support. Closing the door leaves it dark until she conjures floating candles; light from outside is bright when Dumbledore opens it.
entries.model_notes: Preserve storage contents and the temporary candle illumination. The cupboard is near the weighing classroom but not stated to open directly from it.

entries.description: Groups of pupils watch Krum from behind the library bookshelves while others read; their giggling is audible enough to distract Hermione.
entries.model_notes: Establishes shelving used as visual cover and shared reading space, without a complete shelf plan.

entries.description: Third-years and older are permitted a village visit. Harry and Hermione walk into Hogsmeade, visit Honeydukes and the Three Broomsticks, and see the street towards its far end. Outside Honeydukes Harry backs against its wall to avoid Rita passing from the pub.
entries.model_notes: Boundary-visit context and local proximity only; no tunnel is traversed in this visit and no precise shop-to-pub distance is given.

entries.description: The pub is densely crowded with Hogwarts pupils and other magical visitors. Tables extend into a corner where Harry and Hermione sit; drinks are bought separately and Rosmerta collects glasses among the tables.
entries.model_notes: Village destination context only. Do not turn this into a full unrelated village inventory or infer exact floor dimensions.

entries.description: Moody recognises Harry beneath his Invisibility Cloak in the pub and states that his eye can see through such cloaks.
entries.model_notes: A magical visibility exception relevant to stealth routes throughout the school. This is observed recognition plus a reported explanation, not general transparency to every observer.

entries.location: Night route from castle to carriage
entries.description: Harry descends the dark lawn towards lights in Hagrid’s cabin. The nearby Beauxbatons carriage is illuminated inside, and Maxime’s voice is audible as he knocks at the cabin. Hagrid then leads him from the cabin to the carriage and around the edge of the horse paddock.
entries.temporal: Late November 1994, night before first-task preparations
entries.model_notes: Preserve both this auditory description and the earlier two-hundred-yard carriage position without inventing a relocation.

entries.location: Forest perimeter to hidden dragon enclosure
entries.description: Hagrid leads the party around the Forest perimeter until the castle and lake are out of sight, then around a clump of trees to the dragon enclosure. On his return Harry skirts the Forest edge, encounters Karkaroff near the trees, and enters the castle front doors before climbing the marble stairs and continuing to Gryffindor.
entries.model_notes: Tree screening and route ordering are explicit; the exact enclosure bearing and distance from castle are not. The return takes Harry from under fifteen minutes remaining to under five at the castle, but his pace is unknown.

entries.description: Four adult dragons occupy an enclosure fenced with thick wooden planks. About thirty keepers restrain them using chains fixed to heavy leather neck and leg straps; after Stunning them, the keepers secure chains to iron pegs driven deep into the ground. The rearing dragons’ extended mouths are fifty feet high and their fire lights the night.
entries.model_notes: Temporary first-task holding installation, separate from the later spectator arena unless further evidence connects them. Do not use the dragons’ rearing height as fence height.

entries.description: The enclosure holds a blue-grey horned Swedish Short-Snout, a smaller smooth green Welsh dragon, a red Chinese Fireball with facial gold spikes, and a black Hungarian Horntail with bronze tail spikes every few inches. Keepers lay huge granite-grey eggs beside the Horntail.
entries.model_notes: Includes visually distinctive creatures as the enclosure’s dated contents. Charlie supplies breed names and says nesting mothers were requested; biological details do not define permanent terrain.

entries.description: A keeper warns that the dragons can project fire twenty feet and that the Horntail has reached forty feet.
entries.model_notes: Reported hazard ranges for modelling the temporary enclosure; do not confuse these horizontal fire ranges with the narrated fifty-foot rearing height.

entries.description: In the otherwise unlit common room, the fire alone illuminates chairs and a nearby table. Sirius’s head appears in its flames for a face-to-face conversation, then vanishes with a small pop. Footsteps descending the dormitory spiral staircase can be heard from the hearth area; Harry can watch the stair’s bottom across the room.
entries.model_notes: Observed magical fire communication; Sirius reports using a fireplace in another wizard’s house. Preserve the hearth-to-stair acoustic and visual relation without inventing network topology.

entries.description: Harry and Hermione walk three times around the lake before returning to the library.
entries.model_notes: Establishes that a complete walking circuit is possible in this state, not that it is a surfaced path of uniform width or known length.

entries.description: Harry follows Cedric up the marble staircase from the Entrance Hall towards the Charms corridor, where Cedric’s friends enter Flitwick’s classroom. Moody emerges from a nearby classroom and takes Harry to his office.
entries.model_notes: Preserve the upper route and local classroom proximity; the office’s exact floor or direct adjacency to Flitwick’s room is not stated.

entries.description: Harry recalls the same office under Lockhart, with walls covered in smiling self-portraits, and under Lupin, who kept specimens of Dark creatures for lessons.
entries.model_notes: Narrated recollection of changing office contents, not additional rooms or permanent portrait subjects.

entries.description: A large cracked glass Sneakoscope stands on the desk. A humming squiggly golden Secrecy Sensor sits on a small table in a corner. On the wall opposite Harry hangs a Foe-Glass showing indistinct moving figures instead of the room. A large trunk under the window has seven keyholes in a row.
entries.model_notes: Preserve the desk, corner table, wall display and under-window trunk as this occupant’s arrangement; a single view does not fix all their relative distances.

entries.description: Moody says the Secrecy Sensor vibrates at concealment or lies and constantly hums amid school activity. His extra-sensitive Sneakoscope can detect trouble roughly a mile away and has been disabled because it would not stop whistling. He says the Foe-Glass sharpens its hostile figures as danger becomes near.
entries.model_notes: Reported operating rules, not a guarantee that the objects discriminate threats correctly or that every hum is caused by homework lies.

entries.description: Hermione prunes a quivering Flutterby Bush in greenhouse three.
entries.model_notes: A dated plant and lesson placement; no permanent bed arrangement is described.

entries.description: Harry and Hermione use a free classroom for room-crossing Summoning practice. It contains chairs, which Peeves later throws across the room, driving them out after midnight.
entries.model_notes: Unnamed room; do not automatically identify it with another unused classroom in later chapters.

entries.description: At two in the morning Harry practises near the fireplace amid books, quills, upturned chairs, an old Gobstones set and Neville’s toad.
entries.model_notes: Temporary clutter after practice, not the normal furniture layout.

entries.description: McGonagall leads Harry down the front stone steps and around the Forest edge towards the dragon enclosure. A tent erected before the screening trees faces the approach and blocks the dragons from view. Inside are low wooden stools and space for pacing; the audience passes outside, and crowd noise and amplified commentary are audible inside. A short walk from the tent enters the trees.
entries.model_notes: The competition uses the place of the previously visited enclosure; no unexplained relocation is needed. Preserve the approach-facing tent and auditory connection.

entries.description: From the tent Harry passes trees and a gap in the fence into the enclosure. Newly conjured spectator stands rise above him with hundreds of faces looking down. The Horntail crouches at the far end over her eggs on hard ground, cutting yard-long gouges with her tail.
entries.model_notes: Explicitly adds stands to the earlier holding site. The yard measurement is gouge length, not arena size or depth.

entries.location: First-task aerial clearance and Summoning route
entries.description: The summoned Firebolt approaches behind Harry around the edge of the woods and enters the enclosure. Harry flies high above the dragon, circles and dives, then flies over and back across the stands to land near the enclosure entrance.
entries.model_notes: Observed open aerial route and magical object delivery from the castle. The text does not show the Firebolt’s entire path out of its storage place. The shimmering view before arrival is Harry’s stressed perception, not a confirmed magical barrier.

entries.description: A second tent outside the enclosure serves as first aid. It is divided into cubicles by canvas; Cedric’s sitting silhouette is visible through a partition. Pomfrey moves from Harry’s area to the adjacent treatment space.
entries.model_notes: Separate from the champions’ waiting tent. Preserve translucent canvas partitions without inventing their number or furniture type.

entries.location: First-task terrain changes in other trials
entries.description: Ron reports that Cedric Transfigured a rock in the arena into a dog, while Krum’s eye spell caused his dragon to trample and crush about half the real eggs.
entries.model_notes: Reported earlier rounds; the rock supplies a terrain object and the eggs record temporary damage. Harry did not directly see those rounds.

entries.description: After the Horntail is removed, five judges are visible at the opposite end of the enclosure in raised seats draped in gold. They display scores as large magical numerals in the air.
entries.model_notes: Visibility is obstructed by the dragon until removal. The seats are raised but their supporting structure and height are unstated.

entries.description: After revisiting the champions’ tent Harry and Ron return around the Forest edge and pass the clump of trees which screened the first dragon sighting before continuing to the castle.
entries.model_notes: Confirms the same screening clump on the return route; Rita’s hiding place is temporary.

entries.description: After Ron releases Pigwidgeon from an Owlery window, the owl drops twelve feet before recovering flight.
entries.model_notes: Establishes at least twelve feet of unobstructed descent outside that opening, not its total elevation above ground.

entries.description: Cakes and flagons of pumpkin juice and Butterbeer cover common-room surfaces. Fireworks fill the air with stars and sparks, and Dean’s new banners depict Harry flying around the Horntail and Cedric with his head aflame.
entries.model_notes: Temporary party dressing. The open golden egg adds a loud screeching sound later in the scene, but is a carried task prop rather than architecture.

entries.location: Castle and lake in early winter
entries.description: Wind and sleet arrive in December. The castle is draughty but has thick walls and fires; on the lake the Durmstrang ship pitches in high winds with black sails billowing.
entries.model_notes: Observed weather state and contrasting shelter. Harry only supposes the carriage is chilly; that interior temperature is not verified.

entries.description: A trough in a corner of the temporary horse paddock contains single-malt whisky; strong fumes reach the nearby Care of Magical Creatures class.
entries.model_notes: Dated paddock fixture and an acoustic/olfactory proximity cue; no trough dimensions are given.

entries.description: In the windy pumpkin patch Hagrid tries to shut ten nearly six-foot Skrewts into enormous boxes lined with pillows and fluffy blankets. They break out, leaving smouldering box wreckage. One blasts fire that withers nearby pumpkin plants; nine others are restrained and tied up.
entries.model_notes: Record before-and-after box state and plant damage, not a permanent ruined garden.

entries.location: Hagrid’s cabin rear access and garden fence
entries.description: Pupils flee the pumpkin patch through the cabin’s back door and barricade it. Harry and Ron retreat against an outside cabin wall, while Rita watches by leaning on Hagrid’s garden fence. Pupils inside watch through the glazed cabin windows.
entries.model_notes: Connects pumpkin patch, rear door, exterior wall, garden fence and outward window views. The fence is not described as a defensive perimeter.

entries.description: Leaving Trelawney’s room, Harry and Ron regain fresher air on the staircase beneath it.
entries.model_notes: A relative air-quality observation supporting the perfumed, enclosed classroom state; no additional vent or doorway is established.

entries.description: Ron watches Krum from behind bookshelves and finds six or seven girls hidden in the next row of books doing the same.
entries.model_notes: Adds multiple neighbouring shelving rows and inter-row hiding space without determining their number or alignment.

entries.description: Hermione leads Harry and Ron from the Gryffindor portrait corridor down through six floors, then down the marble staircase into the Entrance Hall. Turning left at its foot, they take the door Cedric used and descend a flight of stone steps into a broad, brightly torch-lit stone corridor decorated mainly with cheerful food paintings.
entries.model_notes: Left is from the descending-stair viewpoint, consistent with the earlier door on the staircase’s right when viewed from the Hall. This corridor differs from Snape’s gloomy dungeon approach; do not merge them.

entries.description: A painting showing a gigantic silver fruit bowl stands partway down the corridor. Tickling its huge green pear makes it wriggle and laugh, then transform into a large green door handle; pulling the handle opens the concealed kitchen door.
entries.model_notes: This directly observed operation confirms Fred’s earlier directions in this chapter. Keep the handle transformation and opening action distinct.

entries.description: The kitchen is an enormous high-ceilinged room as large as the Great Hall above it, with stone walls and a flagged stone floor. Glittering brass pots and pans are piled around the walls. A great brick fireplace occupies the far end, with a stool by it.
entries.model_notes: Explicit scale relation to the Great Hall and far-end fireplace placement; no numeric dimensions or ceiling construction are supplied.

entries.description: Four long wooden kitchen tables stand exactly beneath the corresponding four house tables in the Great Hall. They are bare after dinner. At least a hundred house-elves in Hogwarts-crested tea-towels occupy the kitchen, serve tea on a silver tray, and gather at the door when visitors leave.
entries.model_notes: Table alignment is narrated as an observation. No separate fifth staff-service table is described; do not silently add one.

entries.description: Harry supposes that before dinner the lower tables carried the dishes which were then sent through the ceiling to their counterparts in the Great Hall.
entries.model_notes: Explicitly Harry’s deduction from the observed alignment and timing; the actual transfer is not witnessed in this scene.

entries.description: A large cage of guinea-fowl and transformed guinea-pigs stands on McGonagall’s desk. Homework is written on the blackboard, visible from the pupils’ working area including seats at the back.
entries.model_notes: The cage is a lesson prop; the desk and blackboard are classroom fixtures. No room shape is given.

entries.description: McGonagall announces that the Great Hall ball runs from eight until midnight on Christmas Day, open to fourth-years and above and to younger invited partners; the champions and partners open the dancing.
entries.model_notes: Reported rules and scheduled use before the event, not confirmation of a room layout.

entries.location: Sheltered work area behind Hagrid’s cabin
entries.description: For the final Care of Magical Creatures lesson of term pupils shelter behind the cabin at a trestle table, preparing Skrewt food with knives and a large metal bowl.
entries.model_notes: A rear outdoor work area; the cabin itself provides shelter without establishing a roofed outbuilding.

entries.description: Everlasting icicles hang from the marble staircase banisters. Twelve Great Hall Christmas trees carry luminous holly berries and real hooting golden owls. Suits of armour sing carols when passed; Peeves hides inside them and adds rude lyrics until Filch removes him.
entries.model_notes: Dated decorations and triggered armour audio. Icicles are magical persistent decorations, not evidence of a frozen interior.

entries.description: Moaning Myrtle haunts the girls’ toilets on the second floor.
entries.model_notes: Narratorial identification of location and level. No bathroom plan is supplied in this paragraph.

entries.description: Hermione leaves the common room by the girls’ staircase, later described as the route towards the girls’ dormitories.
entries.model_notes: Adds a staircase beyond the previously noted girls’ dormitory doorway; does not specify number of flights.

entries.description: The Gryffindor password has changed to Fairy lights and the Fat Lady wears a new tinsel hairband as her portrait opens.
entries.model_notes: Dated access credential and portrait decoration, not a permanent password.
